\chapter{Village and Shop Complete Ten}
\label{ch:gu-village-shop-ten}
\hlchaptermodality{27}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can hear, say, read, and write ten concrete Gujarati words, including village and shop.}

Village and shop enter meaning-first, then mix with the prior eight words before a non-compensatory four-skill payoff.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[gām]{\gu{ગામ} — hear village first}

\label{lesson:GU-C23-hear-gaam}



\begin{quote}
Recall \emph{shahar}, city. Now listen twice: \textbf{gām}. It means \textbf{village}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Choose city or village as you hear \emph{shahar} or \emph{gām}, then say \emph{gām} once.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english-gujarati/village}{Cambridge: village}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[shahar — shāḷā — rasto]{The three-word route returns at R1}

\label{lesson:GU-R23-route-three-r1}



\begin{quote}
Keep four scores. Each score needs \textbf{3/3}; strength in one skill cannot replace a miss in another. Check and retry only a missed item.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\textbf{Listening — meaning from sound}

Listen once: \emph{shāḷā — rasto — shahar}. Record the listening score before any repair.

\textbf{Speaking — sound from meaning}

Say the three meaning cues without reading a Gujarati model. Record speaking separately.

\textbf{Reading — a cold shuffled row}

Read once before checking. Record the reading score on its own.

\subsection*{Writing — from meaning, with every model covered}
Do not copy from the reading row. Record writing separately, then repair only a missed word.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Which four scores must stand separately? (\textbf{Listening, speaking, reading, and writing.})
